preview: Interview experience for the Technical Analyst Summer Internship at Deutsche Bank covering the online coding round, technical interview, HR round, and professional fitness round.
content: Deutsche Bank Interview Experience. Technical Analyst Summer Internship. Arvind Mundhe, B.Tech IT’23. Online Coding Round(18 September 2021) HackerEarth coding challenge. The total time was 90 minutes. There were 2 coding questions and some MCQs based on CS fundamentals. Only IT/CS students were allowed to attempt the test. 1st coding question (10 test cases, 20 marks) 2nd coding question (15 test cases, 30 marks) 10 MCQs (40 marks) Total marks 90 I solved both the coding questions (passed all the test cases). And I was sure about 8-9 MCQs. Coding question 1 It was a variation of the 0/1 knapsack problem. I was able to solve it using the greedy approach. Given an array of different unsorted integers, an integer k and an int d(number of available operations) We were supposed to return the number of maximum possible multiples using the d number of operations. Where one operation means you can increment a particular element by one. For example, arr = 4 1 5 7 3 9 8 K = 4 D = 5 I solved this question by making an array of required operations per element to convert it into a multiple. arrReq = 0 3 3 1 1 3 0 Then I sorted this array arrReq = 0 0 1 1 3 3 3 Then I traversed the arrReq and maintained a counter variable (ans). When we came across 0 that means the number is already a multiple of k (in this case 4) So for 0, I incremented ans variable by one (we already have a multiple of 4 without any operation) Then for non zero numbers, I checked if we have the required number of operations left for turning that element into a multiple of 4 If yes, Then I incremented ans by one and updated the remaining available operations. And after traversing I returned the ans. Coding question 2 Given an array representing the chemical reactive powers of different reactants. And an int desired result. We were supposed to choose any 2 reactants such that the difference between their reactive powers should be close to the desired result. That is, we have to select reactants with diff as close as possible to the desired_result and maximum output(maximum summation). I don’t remember how they framed the question but it all boiled down to find the pair that satisfied both of the above conditions. I sorted the array, Traversed the array from the end using 2 for loops. maintained a min difference variable whenever the diff between the pair was closer to the desired result, I updated the answer variable to the summation of the powers. This solution passed 10/15 test cases. Then I changed the code to return the ans whenever the diff between the pair was equal to the desired result. As we are traversing from the end, the summation is going to be maximum. This code passed 15/15 test cases. Results of the Coding test were announced on 3rd October. 3 students were shortlisted for the interviews. 2 from CS and 1 from IT. Shortlisted candidates were asked to attend a Pre-Placement talk session. As one candidate from CS was already selected for an internship, Only 2 people were there for the interviews. Technical Interview (45 Minutes) My interview started at 3:00 PM. The interviewer asked me how was I feeling, I told him I was nervous. Then he asked me to play guitar for him. I sang a song for him. Then he started asking technical questions. He asked me what are Database Management Systems? How do we implement isolation in DBMS? I first made sure if he was talking about the isolation from the ACID properties. Then I explained what is Isolation before answering the actual question. Then I told him about the locks(shared and exclusive) and how it is analogous to the race condition in Operating System and the analogy between locks and semaphores and mutex. Then explained how semaphores work. He asked me to write a SQL query to print only odd rows from the table. So I asked him which rows he wanted and if he wants rows with odd number IDs. He said It’s up to you. After thinking a bit I gave this answer, SELECT empName FROM EMPLOYEES WHERE ID%2==1; Then he asked me if I can do it using the MOD function and what if there are no IDs, So I gave this answer, SELECT empName FROM EMPLOYEES WHERE MOD(ROWNUMBER,2) != 0; Then he asked me to rate my C++ skills (looking at my resume) I said 9/10 then he smirked but I proceeded to tell him how I know how to use the C++ STL library properly, and how confident I am about using C++. Then he asked me to explain runtime polymorphism. I explained to him in detail about Dynamic polymorphism and then proceeded to tell him about polymorphism is one of four pillars of the OOPS paradigm. then explained static polymorphism too ;p Then we moved to Java, He asked me if I know java, I said I am aware of the syntactical differences but have no idea of the java collections framework. Then he asked me about abstract keyword, He said is there anything called abstract in C++? I answered NO and told him we don’t use this terminology in C++, and we can call functions that have pure virtual functions as abstract classes. And then explained what is the abstract keyword is based onin the context of Java and explained virtual functions and pure virtual functions. Then he asked me what is sleep(); I answered the question and then he asked me if I know how sleep(); is implemented behind the scenes. I tried to explain using the analogy between the future.delayed from Dart and explained to him how I used it in one of my projects for animating the swapping action. (asynchronous programming) So he was convinced. Then he said as only 3 people were shortlisted for the interviews, you must be very good at problem-solving. I said I practice well that’s it. Then he asked me if I wanted an easy question, I said whatever you want. Then he asked me an easy question, He asked me to print the occurrences of letters in my name. I asked if I should treat the lower case and upper case letters differently and then again he said consider whatever you want. I told him about the frequency array method and how it consumed more space, and then told him I’ll directly explain the unordered_map approach and after explaining I wrote the code and told him what will be the output. Then he asked me to delete the kth last node from a linked list. I explained the naive approach first, which is to find the number of nodes and then move to the node which is just before the node which is to be deleted. Then I explained the two-pointer method, In which we move one pointer k nodes ahead and then start moving both the pointers one by one and then when the further pointer reaches the last node, The first pointer points to the node behind the node which is to be deleted. He was satisfied and did not ask me to code it. Then we had a brief discussion about my projects. The motivation behind my sorting visualizer project and why I named it Project Cliche. Then we talked about my chatting app and how it was different from existing chatting apps. Then we had an informal discussion about the idea behind making another chatting app. Then he asked me if I am given a choice what domain would I like to work on? I said web dev as I am currently learning web dev and would like to explore new things. Then I said I would like to integrate AI/ML into web dev. Then he asked me how sound am I with python? I said I am well versed with it but I will need to brush up a bit and it’ll take hardly a week. Then we talked about automation using Python and how Python is a good language for automation because of many libraries. Then he asked if I had any questions for him. I do not suggest asking this question but I asked him what made him stay in Deutsche bank. Then asked him how they assign domains and projects. Then he said he laughed and told how the process of assigning projects is so random and said,”Jo bhagya me likha hai wahi milega”. And then it was over. Other than technical stuff (we were vibing). He had said treat me like your friend. And after cracking some lame jokes on the life of a software engineer we were vibing. I received a message saying I shortlisted for round 2 at 5:45 PM. They shortlisted 1 candidate for the 2nd round. HR interview. HR interviews in Deutsche bank are generally 45 minutes long. But I was given a window of 20 Minutes. The interview started at 6:45 PM. The interviewer asked me to introduce myself and asked what I know about Deutsche bank. Then asked me why a software engineer should join a banking company. We discussed how technology is an enabler in the banking business. Then he asked why would I be a good fit in Deutsche Bank. I was confused and could not answer this question well. In the end, he asked if I wanted to ask him anything, I asked why should I join Deutsche bank? And how is Deutsche Bank is different than other banks like Barclays, etc? Then I asked him What is the role of a software engineer in Deutsche bank and about the environment at Deutsche bank. Will I get to learn new things, new technology, etc? This interview ended in only 15 minutes. Then I was waiting for the results of the HR interview as these are elimination rounds. I did not get any updates till 9:23 PM. At 9:23 PM I received a phone call from HR and she asked me about the interviews and for how long they were conducted. And she asked me if I got the link for round 3 that is the Professional Fitness interview. Then she sent me the link and asked me if I could join ASAP. Professional Fitness Interview. This round is also generally 45 minutes long. My interview started at 9:45 PM. I was asked to introduce myself ( prepare a good script! ). Then he asked about my family background and if I play guitar professionally, I said I can play professionally but it’s just a hobby for me. Then he asked what are data structures and why and how we use them. Then he asked me a coding question, Given a list of a huge number of strings, I was supposed to sort them for feeding them to another function for further processing. I asked on what basis am I supposed to sort the strings. He said the number of characters, Then I asked, do white spaces count? After thinking a bit I proposed we create a map of strings and their lengths. And then sort it or we could make an ordered map. Then he asked how would I handle strings of the same length? I said we could have some secondary basis for strings of the same length but it wasn’t the answer he was looking for. I said we make a set of pairs containing the actual string and then provide a comparator that sorts on the basis of length and not alphabetically. After discussing how key-value pairs work, we came to a final conclusion, that we use a multi-map with lengths of strings as keys and the actual strings as values and he was satisfied. Then he asked if I had any questions for him. I said,” I tend to ask way many questions and take time to learn things properly, Given that, will I get a proper environment for learning and developing myself as a software engineer?” He answered this question very well and then I said I would enjoy working at Deutsche bank. This concluded the interview. Deutsche Bank selected only one student from VJTI for their Summer Internship program 2021 and I was lucky to be that one student. Resources:- DSA For theory, I watched Abdul Bari’s DSA series. Youtube. For problem-solving, In the beginning, I tried Hackerrank. After getting 5 stars in C++ and problem solving I started using InterviewBit, I reached level 9 there and then stopped. Then I started solving daily 7-8 problems. 3-4 from Leetcode. Leetcode is my personal favourite, It’s concise and has a great variety of problems. Tips:- Your approach matters more than the solution. Think out loud. ( In front of the interviewer ;p ). Practice explaining every line of code to yourself while writing code. I used to practice by explaining my approaches to my friend I used to discuss 2-3 problems with my friends every day. C++ STL is VVV IMP and Java collections too. Practice calculating the time and space complexity whenever you think of an approach. Learn the trade-offs between time and space complexity. (how you can reduce time complexity using some space). OOPs I studied OOPs concepts from lots of different sources, GFG, W3Schools, Youtube, etc. Learn a single concept from various sources so that you’ll get a clear idea of the concept. Operating systems I read bedtime stories on operating systems 2 times. Use it to revise OS. Gate smashers on youtube provides a deep understanding but is very time-consuming. GFG is great too. Having crystal clear concepts is very important for OS. DBMS I started practicing queries on HackerRank, Then moved to InterviewBit. W3Schools for theory and for SQL. Gate Smasher again but still very time-consuming. Normalization by StudyTonight (Youtube). Regularly going through the COC archives helped a lot. If you have any queries, feel free to contact me on LinkedIn Would be happy to help! Believe in yourself and keep working hard!!!!
